campaigns.hook: Before you commit to an accuracy SLA on your AP automation feature, check whether your parser reports field-level or document-level accuracy. The difference matters.

sample_copy.headline: Accuracy SLAs and document parsing: what to verify before you ship
sample_copy.body: Document-level accuracy hides field-level failures. A parser that gets 95% of documents "right" can still drop tax fields or misread line-item totals at a rate that breaks three-way match. When evaluating a parser for production AP automation, ask for: field-level exact-match rates, per-field confidence scores, and p95 latency at your expected volume. DocParse publishes all three. The benchmark methodology is open.

sample_copy.headline: Designing a document ingestion pipeline with a confidence-threshold fallback
sample_copy.body: When a parser returns a confidence score below your threshold, the question is not whether to flag the document — it is what happens next. This post covers how to wire a human-review queue into an AP automation pipeline: where to set the threshold, how to route flagged documents, and how to measure the cost of review against the cost of downstream errors. DocParse exposes per-field confidence scores and a configurable fallback so the routing logic stays in your code, not ours.

campaigns.hook: The accuracy number your OCR vendor quotes is probably document-level. Here is what field-level accuracy means and why it changes the calculation.

sample_copy.headline: Field-level vs. document-level OCR accuracy — why the distinction matters for AP automation
sample_copy.body: Document-level accuracy counts a document as correct if most fields parse correctly. Field-level accuracy counts every field independently. For AP automation, the relevant metric is field-level: a missed tax field or a transposed line-item total causes a downstream reconciliation failure regardless of how the rest of the document parsed. When evaluating parsers, ask for field-level exact-match rates on a dataset that matches your document mix. We published ours on a 5,000-invoice set if you want a reference point.
